journal: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
title: Capsule-inferenced Object Detection for Remote Sensing Images
categories: Journal: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
summary: Frequent and accurate object detection based on remote sensing images can effectively monitor dynamic objects on the Earth's surface. While the Detection Transformer (DETR) offers a simple encoder-decoder structure and a direct set prediction approach to object detection, it falls short in complex remote sensing scenes where entity information and relative positions between objects are critical to target reasoning. Notably, the DETR model's feedforward neural network (FFN) relies on weighted summation for target reasoning, disregarding interactive feature information, which is a major factor affecting detection effectiveness. To address these shortcomings, we propose a DETR-based detection model called (CI_DETR), which uses capsule inference to improve remote sensing object detection. Our approach adds a Multi-level Feature Fusion module to the DETR network, allowing the network to learn how to spatially alter features at different levels, preserving only beneficial information for combination. In addition, we introduce a capsule reasoning module to mine entity information during inference and more effectively model the hierarchical correlation of internal knowledge representation in the neural network, consistent with the thinking model of the human brain. Lastly, we employ a sausage model to measure the similarities and differences of capsules, projecting them onto a curved surface for nonlinear function approximation and maximum preservation of the local responsiveness of capsule entities. Our experiments on public datasets confirm the superior detection performance of our proposed algorithm relative to many current detectors.

title: Dual-domain perception network for small object detection in UAV aerial images
summary: Aerial object detection based on Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) is crucial for applications such as mapping, logistics, and agriculture. However, UAV aerial scenarios contain numerous small objects with limited visual information, which are easily overwhelmed by complex background, posing significant challenges for detectors. To address this problem, we propose a Dual-Domain Perception Network (DDPNet) that comprehensively enhances small object representation through joint spatial- and frequency-domain perception, comprising three core modules: Global-Local Context Modeling Module (GLCMM), Frequency-Domain Understanding Module (FDUM), and Selective Feature Fusion Module (SFFM). GLCMM models global object-scene relationships to adaptively capture foreground-relevant context. FDUM employs Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) with selective feature extraction and adaptive weighting to enhance small object discrimination against complex background. SFFM adaptively fuses spatial- and frequency-domain features, reinforcing small object cues while suppressing irrelevant background interference. DDPNet achieves mAPs of 58.1%, 40.7%, and 62.2% on AI-TOD, VisDrone-DET, and TinyPerson datasets, respectively, surpassing state-of-the-art detectors and demonstrating its effectiveness and robustness in small object detection.

journal: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
title: Effective Infrared Small Target Detection Utilizing a Novel Local Contrast Method
categories: Journal: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
summary: Effective detection of small targets plays a pivotal role in infrared (IR) search and track applications for modern military defense or attack. Consequently, an effective small IR target detection algorithm based on a novel local contrast measure (NLCM) is proposed in this letter. Initially, difference of Gaussian band-pass filter is employed to enhance target and suppress background clutter. Then, a segmentation operation is implemented to obtain IR local regions of fixed size larger than general IR small target size. Finally, the salient map is obtained using the NLCM, and an adaptive threshold is applied to extract the target region. Experimental results on two real sequences show that the proposed method has better detection performance compared with conventional baseline methods.

journal: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
title: Infrared Moving Small-Target Detection Using Spatial–Temporal Local Difference Measure
categories: Journal: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
summary: Effectiveness and false alarm (FA) suppression are key issues in infrared (IR) moving small-target detection. In this letter, we propose a novel spatial-temporal local difference measure (STLDM) algorithm to detect a moving IR small target. The method we propose involves three steps. First, we block off three frames in a certain range of time (temporal) domain. Next, in a 3-D spatial-temporal domain, we analyze the local grayscale intensity difference of the small targets moving between the three frames and calculate the difference between the grayscale intensity in the center area and the grayscale intensity in the eight directions in the area surrounding the target. Finally, we segment the small target in a detection result map. The results of our experiment demonstrate that our proposed STLDM method has a higher rate of detection of IR moving small targets, as well as fewer FAs than other existing methods.

journal: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
title: Infrared Small Target Detection Utilizing the Multiscale Relative Local Contrast Measure
categories: Journal: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
summary: Infrared (IR) small target detection with high detection rate, low false alarm rate, and high detection speed has a significant value, but it is usually very difficult since the small targets are usually very dim and may be easily drowned in different types of interferences. Current algorithms cannot effectively enhance real targets and suppress all the types of interferences simultaneously. In this letter, a multiscale detection algorithm utilizing the relative local contrast measure (RLCM) is proposed. It has a simple structure: first, the multiscale RLCM is calculated for each pixel of the raw IR image to enhance real targets and suppress all the types of interferences simultaneously; then, an adaptive threshold is applied to extract real targets. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can deal with different sizes of small targets under complex backgrounds and has a better effectiveness and robustness against existing algorithms. Besides, the proposed algorithm has the potential of parallel processing, which is very useful for improving the detection speed.

journal: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
title: M2FNet: Multi-modal fusion network for object detection from visible and thermal infrared images
categories: Journal: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
summary: Fusing multi-modal information from visible (VIS) and thermal infrared (TIR) images is crucial for object detection in fully adapting to varied lighting conditions. However, the existing models usually treat VIS and TIR images as independent information and extract corresponding features from separate networks due to the scarcity of training data with labeled instances from both VIS and TIR registration images. To fill this gap, a novel Multi-Modal Fusion NETwork (M2FNet) based on the Transformer architecture is proposed in this paper, which contains two effective modules: the Union-Modal Attention (UMA) and the Cross-Modal Attention (CMA). The UMA module aggregates multi-spectral features from VIS and TIR images and then extracts multi-modal features via a convolutional neural network (CNN) backbone. The CMA module is designed to learn cross-attention features from VIS and TIR pairwise features by Transformer architecture. Evaluation results by the mean average precision (mAP) metric show that the M2FNet method significantly advances the baseline methods trained using only VIS or TIR images by 10.71 % and 2.97 %, respectively. The increments in mAP are observed in the M2FNet method compared with the existing multi-modal methods on two public datasets. Sensitivity analysis of eight illumination thresholds shows that the M2FNet method presents robustness performance on varied illumination conditions and achieves the maximum increase in accuracy of 25.6 %. Moreover, this method is subsequently applied to a new testing dataset, VI2DA (Visible-Infrared paired Video and Image DAtaset), observed by diverse sensors and platforms for testing the generalization ability of object detectors, which will be publicly available at https://github.com/TIR-OD/Datasets.

journal: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
title: Marine Ship Detection Algorithm Based on Adaptive Feature Extraction and Multiscale Feature Weighted Selection Fusion
categories: Journal: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
summary: Accurate identification of marine ship categories is of great significance for tasks such as maritime traffic control and criminal activity prevention. However, due to the small inter-class differences among marine ships and the potentially enormous intra-class differences under different scenarios, the model fails to correctly learn category discrimination features. This further affects the training efficiency of the detection network and reduces the model's classification performance. To address the problems of marine ship shape differences and marine ship size variations caused by imaging positions in high-resolution remote sensing images, we propose a marine ship detection algorithm based on adaptive feature extraction and multi-scale feature weighted fusion(SDAMNet). Considering the characteristics of marine ship targets in remote sensing images, the algorithm introduces an adaptive feature extraction module to adapt to the shape of marine ships, thereby enhancing the model's ability to extract features. Meanwhile, we also design a multi-scale feature weighted selection and fusion module, which uses high level features as weights for low-level features and combines information from different levels to obtain accurate location information and semantic information, enhancing feature representation. Experiments on Level 1 of the shipRSImageNet dataset demonstrate that the joint deployment of AFEM and MSFPN yields gains of 3.85%, 1.85%, and 1.88% in mAP50, mAP75, and mAP50:95 over the baseline, respectively. Ablation experiments on the HRSC2016 dataset corroborate this synergy: combining both modules achieves improvements of 1.66%, 3.32%, and 3.94% in mAP50, mAP75, and mAP50:95 over the baseline, with the pronounced gain at the stricter mAP75 threshold indicating enhanced localization precision, thereby verifying the generalization of the proposed method across different datasets.
